I will keep my land in the wheat-maize rotation this year. In Quzhou, that is the most familiar and steady way for me to farm, and I care first about grain yield, selling easily, and not taking on extra risk. I will not split too much land into specialty crops, because I want work I know well and a plan I can manage with my family and the tools I already have.

So on my land, I will finish the winter wheat that is already in the field, then I will plant summer maize right after wheat harvest. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable emergence and better yield. I will fertilize enough to protect output, but not push too hard because fertilizer costs money. I will irrigate at the key times, especially for wheat in spring and maize after sowing and around big growth stages. I will spray pesticides only when needed for the common local problems, because I want to control damage but also avoid wasting cash. For tillage, I will use ploughing before wheat where I need better soil turning, and rotary tillage for maize after wheat because it is faster and fits the tight season.
